record.resolution: Oman publicly confirmed the planned Gulf-Iran meeting existed, then postponed it. No matching public Omani confirmation of the substantive Iranian route/fee/sovereignty formulations or a signed reopening agreement was established by this cutoff.

record.observed_state: Oman publicly confirmed the planned Gulf-Iran Hormuz meeting and announced its postponement. Iranian officials said some regional countries requested delay and Tehran and Muscat jointly decided to postpone; that attribution to particular Gulf states was not independently established.

AP, citing a Gulf official, reported that Saudi Arabia submitted amendments to the emerging Hormuz proposal over long-term GCC implications. Saudi primary text of the amendments was not public in the reviewed evidence.
A U.S. State Department official said Israel and Lebanon are expected to meet in Rome in October under the U.S.-brokered security framework, with ambassador-level contacts expected beforehand.

record.disposition: The East-West pipeline remained closed through the weekend after the Sep. 11 Iraqi-origin drone attack. Saudi buyers told Reuters that Yanbu stocks could sustain exports for roughly five to seven days if the line remained shut. Exact damaged facilities and the official repair timeline remained unresolved at this cutoff.

record.evidence: Reuters reported the pipeline remained closed throughout the weekend; Yanbu stock cover was estimated at roughly five to seven days if the shutdown persisted.

record.claim: Houthis claimed drones and missiles against Saudi targets including a military base while Saudi authorities issued shelter warnings in Abha and Khamis Mushait.
record.evidence_note: Saudi warning activity is established; the Houthi account of specific successful strikes was not independently verified in the reviewed window.

record.evidence: President Trump, asked whether the United States struck the Iranian cargo vessel, said he did not want to say. This is not an admission. Iranian authorities continued blaming an unspecified terrorist enemy, while UKMTO did not attribute the projectile incident.
Trump's refusal to say whether the United States struck the vessel is preserved as an attribution signal, not as an admission or resolution. Attribution remains unresolved.

record.note: Yemen's government-allied National Resistance issued its first comprehensive west-coast toll for the prior four weeks. The Houthi side did not confirm the figures; they are not treated as an independently established casualty balance.
UN estimate reported by AP; later exact IOM count may supersede this estimate without erasing the earlier knowledge state.

record.claim: Iran is calling constantly and wants a deal badly.

record.claimant: Wall Street Journal report citing unnamed U.S. officials; subsequently addressed by Donald Trump
record.evidence_note: Do not convert alleged activity by China-based entities into PRC state participation absent evidence tying a state organ to the conduct.

record.evidence: A report citing unnamed U.S. officials alleged that China-based entities supplied imagery to Iran before and after the Jordan base attack. PRC state involvement was not established in the reviewed evidence.

record.observed_state: Reuters reported Brent up 2.77% at $107.51/bbl and WTI up 2.27% at $102.32/bbl at 2313 GMT after initially rising more than 3%, amid the Saudi pipeline shutdown, Houthi pressure near Bab el-Mandeb and renewed Hormuz vessel risk.
